chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Hakeym and Hammad, from Abu Masrouq, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) asked me about the people of Basra and said to me: 'What are they?' I said, 'Murjiites, Qadiriyya, and Harouriyya (sects)'. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'May the Curse of Allah be upon those religions of the Unbelievers and the Polytheists, those who do not worship Allah upon anything'.
ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the Murjiites and Qadiriyya sects of Basra?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies the dominant theological currents in Basra—Murji'ah, Qadiriyya, and Haruriyya—as deviations that constitute a form of polytheism (shirk) due to their specific distortions of divine attributes and decree. This narration highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the interconnection of belief in God's justice and predestination with true monotheism, viewing theological error as a barrier to correct worship.
